sentences.text: Yinlong is a basal ceratopsian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic of China, representing the earliest known member of this group.
This small herbivore reached a length of 1.2 meters and a body mass of 10 kilograms.
Although it lacks the frill and horns typical of later relatives, Yinlong is still classified as a ceratopsian.
Fossil evidence reveals seven gastroliths preserved within the abdominal cavity of one individual.
The genus name translates to "hidden dragon," a title inspired by the film Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon.
A team of American and Chinese paleontologists, including Xu Xing and Catherine Forster, formally described the species in 2006.
The initial discovery was an exceptionally well-preserved skeleton unearthed in 2004 from the Shishugou Formation in Xinjiang Province.
The specific epithet downsi honors William Randall Downs III, who passed away the year prior to the fossils being found.
Anatomy suggests a bipedal lifestyle, characterized by long robust hindlimbs and shorter three-fingered forelimbs.
A small rostral bone located on the upper jaw serves as the key identifier for its ceratopsian classification.
Unique features on the skull roof link it to Marginocephalia, a group that also includes pachycephalosaurs and ceratopsians.
Researchers note that skull features in Yinlong resemble those of Heterodontosauridae, supporting a hypothesis of close relationship between these groups.
Yinlong lived during the Oxfordian stage of the Late Jurassic, approximately 161.2 to 155.7 million years ago.
A hypothesis linking Heterodontosauridae and Marginocephalia was not supported by subsequent analyses of Yinlong's postcranial anatomy.
